Project overview

The Administrative Building is a completed project that defines the architectural identity of New Tashkent. Designed in a contemporary national style, it incorporates elements of traditional Uzbek ornamentation.

The building serves as the headquarters of the New Tashkent Directorate, where strategic decisions regarding the future development of the city are made.

Its architectural composition combines monumentality with elegance. The façades are decorated with arches and ornamental details

Project history

The Administrative Building was commissioned by the New Tashkent Directorate to establish the city’s first administrative headquarters and create a recognizable civic landmark for the new capital development. From the outset, the client sought a building that would combine efficient public administration with a strong architectural identity reflecting Uzbekistan’s cultural heritage. Following site analysis and design development, the project was completed as the central hub for planning and managing New Tashkent. Today, it serves as the main workplace of the Directorate and a venue for official meetings, exhibitions, and visits by national and international delegations. The building has become an important symbol of the city’s development, reinforcing public confidence in the project and representing the vision of a modern, sustainable, and culturally rooted New Tashkent.
